def find_frames(grid):
    """Find all frames in the grid. A frame is a rectangular border of a single color."""
    frames = []
    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0]) if rows > 0 else 0
    
    for r in range(rows):
        for c in range(cols):
            # Skip background color
            if grid[r][c] == 6:
                continue
            
            # Check if this starts a frame (top-left corner)
            # A frame corner cell must have the same color on two adjacent edges
            color = grid[r][c]
            
            # Check top and left edges going at least 3 cells
            width = min(cols - c, 10)
            height = min(rows - r, 10)
            
            has_left_side = all(grid[r+i][c] == color for i in range(1, width - 1)) if width > 1 else False
            has_top_side = all(grid[r][c+j] == color for j in range(1, height - 1)) if height > 1 else False
            
            if has_left_side and has_top_side and width >= 3 and height >= 3:
                # Try different frame candidates starting from (r, c)
                for f_r in range(r, min(rows, r + 20)):
                    for f_c in range(c, min(cols, c + 20)):
                        if (f_r - r) < 3 or (f_c - c) < 3:
                            continue
                        
                        # Check if (r, c) to (f_r, f_c) forms a complete frame
                        # Top: row r, cols c to f_c
                        # Bottom: row f_r, cols c to f_c  
                        # Left: rows r to f_r, col c
                        # Right: rows r to f_r, col f_c
                        
                        top_ok = all(grid[r][f_c - j] == color for j in range(f_c - c + 1))
                        bottom_ok = all(grid[f_r][c + j] == color for j in range(f_c - c + 1))
                        left_ok = all(grid[r + j][c] == color for j in range(f_r - r + 1))
                        right_ok = all(grid[r + j][f_c] == color for j in range(f_r - r + 1))
                        
                        if top_ok and bottom_ok and left_ok and right_ok:
                            frames.append({
                                'top': r,
                                'bottom': f_r,
                                'left': c,
                                'right': f_c,
                                'color': color
                            })
    
    return frames

def fill_frame(frame, grid, result):
    """Fill the interior of a frame. 3x3 frames get center=7, larger get interior=2."""
    height = frame['bottom'] - frame['top'] + 1
    width = frame['right'] - frame['left'] + 1
    
    # Interior is (top+1, bottom-1) x (left+1, right-1)
    interior_r_start = frame['top'] + 1
    interior_r_end = frame['bottom'] - 1
    interior_c_start = frame['left'] + 1
    interior_c_end = frame['right'] - 1
    
    if interior_r_end < interior_r_start or interior_c_end < interior_c_start:
        return 3  # Don't fill if interior is empty

        for c in range(interior_c_start, interior_c_end + 1):
            if result[r][c] == 6:  # Only fill background cells that are inside the frame
                result[r][c] = fill_value
